provisions.heading: Invention
provisions.text: 'invention' means a new product or process involving an inventive step and capable of industrial application.
provisions.statutory_significance: Defines basic statutory threshold for patentability.

provisions.heading: Inventive Step
provisions.text: 'inventive step' means a feature of an invention that involves technical advance as compared to the existing knowledge or having economic significance or both and that makes the invention not obvious to a person skilled in the art.
provisions.statutory_significance: Statutory standard for non-obviousness and technical advance required to overcome Section 3(e) and 3(p) challenges in herbal formulations.

provisions.heading: Traditional Knowledge Inventions Not Patentable
provisions.text: An invention which in effect is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known component or components is not an invention within the meaning of this Act.
provisions.statutory_significance: Primary statutory bar preventing monopolization of classical Ayurvedic formulations and known herbal properties.

provisions.heading: Mere Admixture Not Patentable
provisions.text: A substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components thereof or a process for producing such substance is not an invention within the meaning of this Act.
provisions.statutory_significance: Mandates technical proof of non-obvious synergistic effect when combining multiple known botanical ingredients.

provisions.heading: Naturally Occurring Substances Not Patentable
provisions.text: The mere discovery of a scientific principle or the formulation of an abstract theory or discovery of any living thing or non-living substance occurring in nature is not an invention.
provisions.statutory_significance: Naturally occurring whole herbs and crude botanicals cannot be patented in isolated form.

provisions.heading: Methods of Treatment Not Patentable
provisions.text: Any process for the medicinal, surgical, curative, prophylactic, diagnostic, therapeutic or other treatment of human beings or any similar treatment of animals to render them free of disease or to increase their economic value or that of their products is not an invention.
provisions.statutory_significance: Methods of treating patients with Ayurvedic remedies cannot be patented in India; claims must be formulated as novel compositions or processes.

provisions.heading: Mandatory Biological Material Source Disclosure
provisions.text: Every complete specification shall fully and particularly describe the invention and its operation or use and the method by which it is to be performed; and disclose the source and geographical origin of the biological material in the specification, when used in an invention.
provisions.statutory_significance: Statutory duty of disclosure for all Ayurvedic patents using Indian botanicals.

provisions.heading: Opposition Ground for Traditional Knowledge Anticipation
provisions.text: Where an application for a patent has been published, any person may oppose the grant on the ground that the complete specification does not disclose or wrongly mentions the source or geographical origin of biological material used for the invention, or that the invention claimed was anticipated having regard to the knowledge, oral or otherwise, available within any local or indigenous community in India or elsewhere.

location.chapter: Chapter V (Opposition to Grant of Patent)

provisions.statutory_significance: Legal mechanism for CSIR and third parties to challenge biopiracy patents.

provisions.heading: Frivolous Inventions & Contrary to Natural Laws
provisions.text: An invention which is frivolous or which claims anything obviously contrary to well established natural laws is not an invention within the meaning of this Act.
provisions.statutory_significance: Excludes unscientific claims and perpetual motion assertions.

provisions.heading: New Form of Known Substance / Enhanced Efficacy
provisions.text: The mere discovery of a new form of a known substance which does not result in the enhancement of the known efficacy of that substance or the mere discovery of any new property or new use for a known substance is not patentable.
provisions.statutory_significance: Requires demonstrated enhanced therapeutic efficacy for botanical derivatives.

provisions.heading: Method of Agriculture or Horticulture Exclusion
provisions.text: A method of agriculture or horticulture is not an invention within the meaning of this Act.
provisions.statutory_significance: Excludes herbal farming, vertical cultivation, and harvesting methods.

provisions.heading: Plants, Animals, Varieties and Species Exclusion
provisions.text: Plants and animals in whole or any part thereof other than micro-organisms; but including seeds, varieties and species and essentially biological processes for production or propagation of plants and animals are not inventions within the meaning of this Act.
provisions.statutory_significance: Excludes living plant species and wild botanicals; protectable under PPV&FR Act 2001.

provisions.heading: Pre-Grant Opposition on Non-Disclosure of Origin
provisions.text: Where an application for a patent has been published, any person may oppose the grant on the ground that the complete specification does not disclose or wrongly mentions the source or geographical origin of biological material used for the invention.

location.chapter: Chapter V (Opposition to Grant of Patent)

provisions.statutory_significance: Ground for opposing grant when biological origin is withheld.

provisions.heading: Residents Not to Apply for Patents Outside India without Prior Permission
provisions.text: No person resident in India shall, except under the authority of a written permit sought in the manner prescribed and granted by or on behalf of the Controller, make or cause to be made any application outside India for the grant of a patent for an invention.

location.chapter: Chapter VII (Provisions for Secrecy of Inventions)

provisions.statutory_significance: Mandatory prior permission for Indian residents filing patents abroad.

provisions.heading: Liability for Contravention of Section 35 or Section 39
provisions.text: If in respect of an application for a patent any person contravenes section 39 the application for patent under this Act shall be deemed to be abandoned and any patent granted shall be liable to be revoked under section 64.

location.chapter: Chapter VII (Provisions for Secrecy of Inventions)

provisions.statutory_significance: Deemed abandonment and patent revocation consequences for Section 39 violations.

provisions.heading: Revocation of Patent on Traditional Knowledge Grounds
provisions.text: A patent may be revoked on the ground that the complete specification does not disclose or wrongly mentions the source and geographical origin of biological material, or that the invention claimed was anticipated having regard to the knowledge, oral or otherwise, available within any local or indigenous community in India or elsewhere.
provisions.statutory_significance: Statutory ground for invalidating patents obtained through biopiracy.
